title: Capital Union Bank - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
summary: Discovery call to understand Capital Union Bank's data residency and compliance requirements for LLM inference. Discussed options (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), data residency, logging retention, HIPAA/GDPR concerns, SOC2, KMS/HSM, on-prem requirements and benchmarks. Agreed to share security pack, architecture notes, and schedule a benchmark POC on dedicated capacity.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya with Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. How's everybody? 
[00:07] Laura Peters: Morning, thanks — Laura from Capital Union, head of compliance. We have Samir and Jen on too. 
[00:15] Diego Alvarez: Great. Quick agenda, we want to understand your stack and constraints for data residency and compliance then map Redwood options. 
[00:23] Samir Khan: Sure, we've been evaluating LLMs for internal assistant and some customer-facing features. Main blocker is where logs and user data live — must be in-country and we need audit trails, and in some cases PHI can't leave our network. 
[00:36] Maya Chen: Understood. High-level we offer Hosted (multi-region hosted API), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in a region/account) and Private (VPC or on-prem). For strict in-country requirements we often recommend Dedicated regional deployment or Private. 
[00:50] Jen Ortiz: Can you elaborate dif between dedicated and private? We worry about maintenance overhead if we go private on prem. 
[00:58] Diego Alvarez: Yeah, decent question. Dedicated is Redwood-managed infra but isolated to your tenant and region — think reserved capacity in a cloud region with VPC peering. Private is customer-managed control plane or full on-prem install, gives you full network and key control but requires ops resources. 
[01:15] Laura Peters: For GDPR, we need a data processing addendum and the ability to show data residency and to handle DSARs. Also retention policy — logs must be retained for seven years for banking audit. 
[01:28] Maya Chen: We have a DPA template and support EU data residency — Hosted can be regionally hosted but note hosted is shared infrastructure; Dedicated pins capacity to a region and you can disable cross-region replication. Private gives you the strongest guarantees. 
[01:43] Samir Khan: About logs — Redwood stores request/response logs for tracing but we can reduce retention or disable storing responses for certain routes? 
[01:52] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have per-route logging controls and the ability to redact or not persist responses. There's also support for redact hooks and token-level hashing. A note: some of the auto transcriber's words — we call it K V cache — sorry K V cache, but sometimes it's logged differently in transcripts. 
[02:07] Laura Peters: We also need HIPAA compliance for a subset of features where insurance data or health claims surface. Do you sign BAAs? 
[02:14] Maya Chen: We do offer HIPAA support on Dedicated and Private deployments; we can sign BAA for Dedicated with specific controls — encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS, audit logs, and restricted access controls. Hosted generally is hard for HIPAA unless it's a dedicated private tenancy. 
[02:28] Jen Ortiz: Key management — do you support customer-managed keys (bring your own key/HSM)? 
[02:33] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we integrate with cloud KMS providers and can support external HSMs for Private. In Dedicated we can do customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and control key rotation policies. 
[02:45] Samir Khan: What about SOC 2 and other certifications — we need artifacts for vendor review. 
[02:50] Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. We can provide our latest report under NDA and also ISO snapshot. We'll share the security pack after this call. 
[03:02] Laura Peters: Audit trail granularity — we need immutable logs with user identity mapping and ability to export to our SIEM. 
[03:10] Diego Alvarez: We support streaming audit logs to your S3 or to SIEM via syslog/HTTP. Logs include request metadata, user IDs, model version, and can be configured to exclude model outputs. You can set retention rules on your side too. 
[03:25] Samir Khan: Data residency nuance — if inference runs in region A but model weights are stored elsewhere, is that an issue? 
[03:32] Maya Chen: Good point — for Dedicated and Private we can ensure model artifacts and KV caches are stored in-region. Hosted might use centralized object stores; for strict regs we'd advise dedicated or private. 
[03:44] Jen Ortiz: For latency-critical paths, we worry about model fallbacks — if primary region unavailable, can requests failover? That may cause cross-border egress. 
[03:53] Diego Alvarez: We support configurable routing policies; failover can be disabled for compliance-sensitive routes. Fallbacks can be to in-region smaller models. 
[04:05] Laura Peters: Regarding logging restrictions — some regulators prohibit retention of certain customer identifiers. Can Redwood mask or tokenise PII at ingest? 
[04:13] Maya Chen: Yes, we offer pre-ingest redaction, PII tokenization, and schema-based redaction. Also can run inference on hashed identifiers. Implementation detail: redaction is a pipeline step in our gateway. 
[04:27] Samir Khan: What about subprocessor list and data transfer agreements for EU? 
[04:31] Maya Chen: We'll share subprocessors and SCCs where applicable. For EU-only data we recommend Dedicated in EU region or Private. 
[04:40] Jen Ortiz: We want the ability to perform an internal security review — is there a checklist? 
[04:45] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have an internal vendor security checklist we can map to; we'll include mapping to your requirements list. 
[04:52] Laura Peters: Can Redwood limit telemetry? We only want basic metrics and no payloads. 
[04:58] Diego Alvarez: You can limit telemetry scope, disable payload collection, and still get cost/latency metrics. Metric-level aggregation versus request-level logs is configurable. 
[05:10] Samir Khan: For proof-of-concept, what's the fastest path? We want to run 10k concurrent short inference tests in-region. 
[05:17] Maya Chen: Easiest is Dedicated reserved capacity in your preferred region — we can provision a small GPU pool and run benchmarks; in some cases we can run a time-bound Private POC if you prefer. 
[05:27] Jen Ortiz: Cost question — how do you present cost guarantees for dedicated? 
[05:31] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with committed throughput and pricing; we can propose a pilot package with capped usage for the POC. 
[05:38] Laura Peters: A couple of nitty bits — can we get data deletion guarantees for test data post-POC? 
[05:44] Diego Alvarez: Yes, we have data deletion APIs and certs for deletion; we can provide deletion logs. 
[05:50] Samir Khan: Any limits on log export size or retention? 
[05:54] Diego Alvarez: No hard limits, it's more about retention policy; export throughput can be tuned. We recommend exporting to your S3 for long-term retention. 
[06:03] Laura Peters: Can you talk about network topology for VPC peering? We need source IPs, ports, and peering process. 
[06:09] Maya Chen: We'll send our VPC peering guide — includes IP ranges, ports (gRPC/HTTPS), and required firewall rules. For Private on-prem we provide a connector. 
[06:19] Jen Ortiz: Are there any known issues with our stack? We're on Azure with ExpressRoute and strict egress. 
[06:26] Diego Alvarez: We have Azure deployments and support ExpressRoute; we can run through the network design with your infra team in a follow-up. 
[06:34] Samir Khan: Regarding BAA and HIPAA — you said dedicated can sign BAA. Do you have customer examples? 
[06:40] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a couple of customers in healthtech on Dedicated; we'll anonymize examples but can share compliance patterns. 
[06:48] Laura Peters: What about access controls — SSO, SCIM, RBAC? 
[06:52] Diego Alvarez: Support for SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls with audit trails. We can restrict role scopes per environment. 
[07:03] Jen Ortiz: Ok, next steps I'd like: security pack, network guide, and a proposal for a dedicated pilot with pricing. 
[07:11] Maya Chen: Happy to. We'll follow up with those. Any other Qs? 
[07:15] Laura Peters: One more — can we get an export of the model versioning policy and model artifact residency? 
[07:20] Maya Chen: We'll include model version policy doc. 
[07:24] Diego Alvarez: Also I'll propose a benchmark plan — target 10k concurrent short calls with in-region Dedicated GPUs. 
[07:32] Samir Khan: Great. Thanks everyone. 
[07:35] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll send notes and action items. 
[07:38] [End of recording]
next_steps: Send security pack (SOC2, DPA, HIPAA guidance) via NDA
Share VPC peering guide and IP ranges
Send Dedicated pilot proposal with pricing and sizing for 10k concurrent inference
Schedule technical deep dive with infra team (network + ExpressRoute)
Provide model residency and versioning doc and deletion certificate
